To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we collected a large cross-domain database of real face images, with 27.002 facial images of selfies (selfportraits) and ID documents (IDs) captured from the major public Brazilian Bank, we developed and proposed a novel cross-domain face matching approach based on deep features and we obtained results on this dataset, with accuracy rates above 93%, demonstrating the robustness of our approach for the cross-domain problem and its feasibility for real banking security systems.

(a) we propose a cross-domain approach to compare faces in ID documents and self-portraits (selfies); (b) the proposed approach is based on deep features obtained from Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), trained on large databases; (c) the results obtained in the experiments demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed approach for real banking security systems; and (d) the proposed approach can also be applied in other security scenarios, in which faces from ID documents are used for user authentication.

we propose a novel deep learning approach for cross-domain face matching, which is robust to the problem of matching faces in ID documents and selfies, and that we collect and publicly release a large cross-domain database, called FaceBank, which is the largest publicly available database of its kind, with more than 27 thousand real facial images of IDs and selfies captured by the systems of the largest bank of Brazil.
In summary, our research is concerned with

(i) the collection of a large face dataset for cross-domain face recognition, (ii) the proposal of a new cross-domain face matching approach, and (iii) the evaluation of the proposed approach on the large collected dataset.

the development of a novel approach to face matching for real banking security systems, which are currently based on the cross-domain problem of comparing faces in IDs and selfportraits (i.e., selfies) of mobile devices.

the development and validation of an automatic approach for face matching based on the analysis of deep features of facial images, in order to support banking systems in the security of transactions and the opening of new checking account.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results achieved with our approach are very promising and show the feasibility of using deep features extracted by CNNs for cross-domain face matching in real banking security scenarios.

the proposed approach can be applied in real banking systems, since it is able to deal with the cross-domain problem, with accuracy rates above 90%, which is the threshold for the acceptance of a biometric system in a real application.

our proposed approach is a promising and reliable solution for cross-domain biometric face matching, and it can be applied in the real security systems of banks, as well as in other applications that require cross-domain face matching.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have proposed an innovative solution to the problem of cross-domain face matching, based on deep features, and we have collected a large database with 27,000 real facial images of IDs and selfies from the systems of a public bank.

the FaceBank database, the proposed cross-domain deep face matching approach, and the obtained experimental results are all very relevant and useful for the research community, and also for the development of real-world applications in banking security systems.
, in the last decade, the use of face for biometrics in banking systems has been growing and the proposed approach, based on deep learning, has shown promising results in cross-domain scenarios.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the context of real banking security systems, the proposed cross-domain approach is able to achieve a good performance in the face matching task, even with the use of only a small amount of training samples.
, with a large enough dataset, deep learning approaches can be applied in real security systems with very high accuracy rates.

deep face matching is a feasible approach for the security of banking systems, and that it can also be used in a large variety of real-world applications, including the verification of the identity of users, the identification of suspects in security videos, and the verification of the authenticity of ID documents.
